exact_witness.interpretation: the focal actor rationally commits before the cue while the interacting system would gain by waiting

endogenous_information_asymmetry_witness.interpretation: identical cue process can generate different information access solely because actors face different opportunity costs of waiting

source_backed_ecological_anchor.male_early_decision: male settlement did not respond detectably to manipulated tit timing and was largely completed before hatching treatment became apparent
source_backed_ecological_anchor.female_later_decision: later female settlement/pairing responded to manipulated tit timing and treatment separation increased later in the season
source_backed_ecological_anchor.caveat: the experiment does not estimate PAYOFF-B delay-cost or information-value parameters

prior_art_boundary: Bauer, McNamara & Barta 2020 already model environmental predictability, information and migration timing
Schneeberger & Taborsky 2020 review costs of acquiring and using social information
value-of-information methods are established in ecology
PAYOFF-B novelty cannot be that waiting for information is costly
retained_candidate_contribution: embed timing-dependent information acquisition into an interacting seasonal game, derive a private-versus-joint value-of-waiting wedge, connect unequal decision deadlines to endogenous information asymmetry, and then link this to topology-dependent coordination memory
claim_boundary: phase-map frequencies are design frequencies, not natural prevalences
canonical delay costs are illustrative payoff units
cue accuracy is an abstract information coordinate
flycatcher source data bytes were not independently reanalysed in this session because current Dryad file downloads require authenticated bearer access
the source-backed experiment anchors timing-dependent cue availability but not the quantitative model parameters
